files.06-manuscript/chapters/ch-011.md:
Sena reached the last well before the salt at first light. The keeper had already drawn the rope up and coiled it on the stone.

"Guild water is paid at the gate," he said. "Not here."

She showed him the courier's knot on her sleeve. He looked at it for as long as it took a mule to drink, then let the rope down again.

By noon the salt had begun to sing under her boots. She kept the sealed letter flat against her ribs and did not look back at the well.
